extracted.intended_audience: FDA employees, regulated parties/interested persons (industry, counsel), and courts
extracted.subtask_description: CFR Part 10 provisions governing judicial review, formal evidentiary hearings, separation of functions/ex parte communications, meetings/correspondence, administrative file documentation, internal review, draft dissemination, advisory opinions, and classification of regulations/recommendations for matters under the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final agency action; exhaustion and ripeness for judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Final agency action exhausts all administrative remedies and is ripe for preenforcement judicial review as of the date of the final decision, unless applicable law explicitly requires that the petitioner take further action before judicial review is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency takes the position that an interested person is affected by, and thus has standing to obtain judicial review of final agency action. It is not appropriate to move to dismiss a suit for preenforcement judicial review of final agency action on the ground that indispensable parties are not joined or that it is an unconsented suit against the United States if the defect could be cured by amending the complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner may object to judicial review in certain matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall object to judicial review of a matter if: (i) the matter is committed by law to the discretion of the Commissioner (e.g., decisions to recommend enforcement actions under specified sections), or (ii) review is not sought in a proper court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include decisions committed to Commissioner discretion such as recommending civil or criminal enforcement under sections 302, 303, and 304 of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review limited to the administrative record
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall take the position that the validity of administrative action must be determined solely on the basis of the administrative record specified in §§ 10.30(i), 10.33(k), 10.35(h), 10.40(g), and 16.80(a) (or the applicable administrative record), and that additional information or views may not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interested person who wishes to rely upon information or views not included in the administrative record shall submit them to the Commissioner with a new petition to modify the action under § 10.25(a). This position applies whether or not the judicial review action includes a declaratory judgment request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests to consolidate petitions / prevent multiplicity of suits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner requests that all petitions for judicial review of a particular matter be filed in a single U.S. District Court and, if petitions are filed in more than one jurisdiction, will take appropriate action to prevent multiplicity of suits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible actions include: (1) requesting transfer/consolidation of suits under 28 U.S.C. 1404(a) or 28 U.S.C. 2112(a); (2) requesting stays of actions in all but one jurisdiction; (3) requesting dismissal of all but one action with suggestion that other plaintiffs intervene; or (4) requesting that one suit be maintained as a class action on behalf of all affected persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and agency response when court finds administrative record inadequate or explanation insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: If a court determines the administrative record is inadequate to support the action, the Commissioner shall decide whether to proceed; if proceeding, the court will be requested to remand to reopen proceedings and record, or the agency may reopen on its own initiative. If the record is adequate but the rationale needs further explanation, the Commissioner shall request further explanation to the court or reopening of the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commissioner concludes the public interest requires the action remain in effect pending further proceedings, the Commissioner will request the court not to stay the matter and shall expedite further administrative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promulgation of regulations/orders after formal evidentiary public hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall promulgate regulations and orders after an opportunity for a formal evidentiary public hearing under part 12 whenever: (1) the subject matter is by statute subject to such an opportunity, and (2) the person requesting the hearing has a right to the hearing and submits adequate justification as required by §§ 12.20–12.22 and other applicable provisions (e.g., §§ 314.200, 514.200, 601.7(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner may also order a formal evidentiary public hearing on any matter whenever it would be in the public interest to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters that statutorily afford opportunity for formal evidentiary public hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: A set list of statutory sections (e.g., sections 401, 403(j), 404(a), 406, 409(c)(d)(h), 501(b), 502(h), 502(n), 512(n)(5), 721(b)(c), Fair Packaging and Labeling Act provisions, sections 505(d)(e), 512(d)(e)(m), 515(g), 351(a) of PHS Act, section 306 debarment provisions, etc.) afford persons an opportunity for a formal evidentiary public hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list 'imparts no right to a hearing where the statutory section provides no opportunity for a hearing' — it identifies the statutory provisions where hearings are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of functions and ex parte communications rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For matters subject to a formal hearing (listed in § 10.50(c)) or to a Public Board of Inquiry, separation of functions applies upon publication of notice: the center responsible is responsible for investigative functions and presentation at hearing but may not participate or advise in the Commissioner's decision except as witness or counsel; there shall be no other communication between center representatives and representatives of the office of the Commissioner concerning the matter before the decision of the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner and Chief Counsel shall designate, by written memorandum filed with Dockets Management Staff, members who may advise either the center or the office of the Commissioner. Those designated to advise one side may not participate or advise in the other side's decision except as counsel in public proceedings. The office of the Commissioner (with advice from anyone other than center representatives and designated counsel) is responsible for agency review and final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions and procedures for communications after separation applies
rubrics_metrics.description: Between the time separation of functions applies and the Commissioner's decision, no person outside the agency may have an ex parte communication with the presiding officer or any person representing the office of the Commissioner concerning the matter, and vice versa; all communications are to be public communications as witness or counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement-related communications by a participant may be submitted as pleadings, served on all participants and filed with Dockets Management Staff. Any written or oral communication contrary to the section must be immediately served on all participants and filed; oral communications must be memorialized and those involved made available for cross-examination if possible. Rebuttal testimony may be permitted and transcribed. Making communications contrary to the section may result in an adverse decision consistent with justice and statute policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for court referrals to the Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: When a court holds in abeyance or refers a matter to the Commissioner for an initial administrative determination under § 10.25(c) or § 10.45(b), the Commissioner shall promptly agree or decline to accept the referral and, whenever feasible, agree and proceed to determine the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In reviewing the matter, the Commissioner may use conferences/meetings under § 10.65, hearings under parts 12–16, Federal Register notices requesting information/views, or other public procedures applicable to the matter. If review results in a proposed rule, §§ 10.40 or 10.50 apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meetings and correspondence between FDA and interested persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Meetings and correspondence may be held between FDA representatives and interested persons on matters within the Commissioner's jurisdiction; action on such meetings/correspondence does not constitute final administrative action under § 10.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner may hold open public meetings (informal, notice of time/place/matters to be discussed) and every person may request a private meeting in agency offices; FDA will make reasonable efforts to accommodate. Requesters may be accompanied by a reasonable number of employees/consultants with whom there is a commercial arrangement. FDA determines which agency representatives will attend; requesters may request but not require attendance of a specific employee. Persons not invited may request a separate meeting. Agency reps should meet all public segments where appropriate, may request meetings be open, and may decline private meetings if public interest demands. Agency reps may not knowingly participate in meetings closed on basis of gender/race/religion. FDA will prepare transcripts/recordings/memoranda when useful and will file memoranda and correspondence in the administrative file; FDA may initiate meetings or correspondence. Advisory committee meetings are subject to part 14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation standards for significant decisions in the administrative file
rubrics_metrics.description: Every significant FDA decision (formal or informal) must have an administrative file containing appropriate documentation of the basis for the decision (evaluations, reviews, memoranda, letters, consultant opinions, minutes, etc.) and the recommendations and decisions of individual employees responsible for handling the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations and decisions must reveal significant controversies or differences of opinion and their resolution. Employees may record individual views in written memoranda placed in the file. Written documents placed in the file must: relate to factual/scientific/legal issues under consideration; be dated and signed by the author; be directed to the file and show all persons who received copies; avoid defamatory or intemperate remarks, undocumented charges, or irrelevant matters; if recording multiple authors' views, be given to other employees; and once completed not be altered or removed (later additions must be new documents). Memoranda not in the administrative file have no status or effect. Employees who worked on the matter have access to the administrative file as appropriate, subject to reasonable restrictions to assure cataloging, availability, and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal agency review of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision of an FDA employee (other than the Commissioner) is subject to supervisory review at the employee's request, on the supervisor's initiative, at the request of an interested person outside the agency, or as required by delegations of authority. The review will be by consultation, review of the administrative file, or both, and ordinarily follows established agency channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors/applicants/manufacturers may request review of scientific controversies by an appropriate scientific advisory panel or advisory committee; denials must briefly state reasons in writing. Interested persons may request internal agency review through established channels; personal review by center directors or the Commissioner will occur to resolve issues not resolvable at lower levels, to review policy matters, in unusual situations requiring immediate review in the public interest, or as required by delegations. Internal review must be based on information in the administrative file; if new information is presented it will be returned for reevaluation at the appropriate lower level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for dissemination and discussion of draft Federal Register notices and regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA representatives may discuss concepts and recommendations with interested persons. Once a notice or proposed regulation will be prepared, general concepts may be discussed; details of a draft proposed regulation may be discussed with a person outside the executive branch only with specific written permission of the Commissioner filed with Dockets Management Staff, and a draft may be furnished to a person only if it is made available to all interested persons by a Federal Register notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After publication of a proposed rule and before preparing a draft final notice, limited discussion per (b)(2) is permitted. Details of a draft final notice/regulation may be discussed only with Commissioner's written permission; a draft final may be furnished only if made available to all by Federal Register notice except as provided in (g) and (j). The final notice or regulation and its preamble will be prepared solely on the basis of the administrative record. Additional technical information needed from outside persons will be requested by FDA in general terms and furnished directly to Dockets Management Staff. If direct discussion of a draft final with an outside person is required, protective procedures (e.g., open public meeting under § 10.65(b) or preparation of a tentative final regulation under § 10.40(f)(6) with additional comment period) will be undertaken to ensure a full and impartial administrative record. After a final regulation is published, FDA may discuss any aspect with an interested person. Certain drafts (food/additive/color/new animal drug regulations) may be furnished to petitioners for technical accuracy, but every meeting must be recorded and filed in Dockets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory opinions: request, form, effect, amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested person may request an advisory opinion on a matter of general applicability; requests will be granted whenever feasible but may be denied for incomplete information, inability to give a reasonable opinion, prior coverage, product-specific matters that do not raise broad policy, or if not in the public interest. Requests must follow § 10.20 and the form set out in § 10.85(b), including concise issues, full facts and legal points, and a certification that all relevant data/views (favorable or unfavorable) are included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement of policy or interpretation in certain documents (Federal Register notices other than text of regs, specified trade correspondence, compliance policy guides, and other documents identified as advisory opinions) will constitute an advisory opinion. An advisory opinion represents the formal position of FDA and obligates the agency to follow it until amended or revoked; the Commissioner may not recommend legal action against a person acting in conformity with an advisory opinion that has not been amended/revoked. In unusual immediate significant danger, the Commissioner may take enforcement action contrary to an advisory opinion only with Commissioner approval, and will expedite amendment/revocation. Advisory opinions may be amended/revoked at any time with notice and public filing; actions undertaken in conformity remain acceptable unless public interest considerations preclude continued acceptance. Interested persons may submit written comments (four copies) for the public file. Advisory opinions may be used to illustrate acceptable/unacceptable procedures in proceedings but not as a legal requirement. Only statements issued in writing under this section constitute advisory opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of FDA documents: regulations, recommendations, and agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA regulations are issued in the Federal Register under § 10.40 or § 10.50 and codified in the CFR; regulations may contain provisions enforceable as legal requirements, or intended only as guidance documents and recommendations, or both. Dissemination of draft notices and regulations is subject to § 10.80.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to regulations, FDA formulates and disseminates recommendations (guidance documents) about matters authorized by but not involving direct regulatory action (e.g., model State/local ordinances or personnel practices). Recommendations are distinct from formal regulations and are addressed elsewhere (see § 10.115).
